regions.region: page 1 title, abstract, author block, and SI availability sentence
regions.finding: The article title and aggregate cobalt-catalyzed Z-selective hydroboration claim were inspected. The paper points to online SI, but workspace association remains unestablished and no SI fact was imported.

Two printed Roush prior-work examples were retained separately: c-C6H11 gives 86% and syn/anti 78:22; n-C8H17 gives 81% and syn/anti 60:40. They are literature examples, not current-paper experiments.
The generic Tsuji Cu/CF3Ar-Xantphos hydroboration is classified as cited prior work with its printed E-selectivity statements; missing yield/conditions remain explicit.
Three Miyaura Pt(dba)2/ligand combinations with distinct R, yields, and Z/E ratios are retained as separate literature-example records.
The generic Co-PNN transformation is classified as the current general scheme; experiment-specific results are assigned to Tables 1 and 2.
The complicated catalyst-1 run and the 2a result map to Table 1 entries 1 and 2 on page 2; narrative evidence is merged into those row records rather than duplicated.

unresolved: Prior-work schemes omit many operational details and contain generic R/R2 groups.
The SI mentioned by the article is not associated in this workspace.

regions.region: page 2 upper-left Table 1 reaction header, entries 1–13, structures, and footnotes
regions.finding: Thirteen independent optimization conditions were retained with row precatalyst/solvent, footnote loadings and times, NMR product yields, isolated 87% result, recoveries, catalyst/activator omission controls, and no-conversion or complicated outcomes. The original image establishes 2/4 umol in footnote a rather than the text-layer mmol OCR.

The prose confirms Table 1 row interpretations, including complicated entry 1, exclusive product/recovery in entry 3, optimized entry 4, solvent effects, and no-conversion entries 12/13; no duplicate narrative records were created.

The prose maps to the Table 2 rows displayed on page 3, including the separate 5 mmol 3a run, functional-group/chemoselectivity statements, 1,1-disubstituted allenes, and bisallene double hydroborations.
Four transformations of Z-4a are mapped to the four Scheme 2 arrows on page 3 and are not duplicated as prose-only records.
The narrative introduces Scheme 3a/3b and proposed Int 1/Int 2-A/Int 3-A; it is linked to one mechanism record rather than treated as isolated preparations.

unresolved: Table 2 maps neither 1.0 nor 0.5 mmol scale to individual ordinary rows.
Scope operational workups and masses are absent from the main text.
Mechanistic intermediates are partly proposed and partly MS-observed.

regions.region: page 3 upper Table 2 header and Z-4a through Z-4p rows
regions.finding: Each displayed product row is a separate substrate-scope experiment with shared HBpin/2b/NaBHEt3/toluene conditions, isolated yield, and footnote overrides. The ordinary 87% Z-4a row and separate 5 mmol/1.16 g/83% repetition are distinct.

regions.region: page 3 Table 2 enallene, 1,1-disubstituted allene, and bisallene rows
regions.finding: Rows 4q–4s, 4t–4x, and 4y–4z were retained separately. Footnote times/loadings/50 °C overrides, Z/E ratios, and the bisallene 2.2-equiv HBpin/6 mol% 2b/12 mol% NaBHEt3 conditions are structured.

Footnote additives/loadings, row-specific reaction times, temperature overrides, isolated-yield basis, and the 5 mmol product mass were assigned to their rows. The shared 1.0 or 0.5 mmol options remain unresolved by row.

Four independent Z-4a derivatizations were retained. The -30 °C-to-room-temperature 6 h and 0 °C-to-room-temperature 3 h/14 h programs are represented as ordered timed transitions, not collapsed into a single temperature.
